why.blast: low — a guard wired into the commit chain, a dead pointer removed from two real files backing three shipped paths, and a prose correction to the parent node. No lifecycle write, no schema change, no behavior change for any loaded plugin.

The non-obvious parts are keying the pointer rule on value shape rather than a key list, and resolving against the plugin root rather than the manifest's own directory; both are bound in the suite because neither is self-evident to a reader of the code.
why.confidence: high — four cold impl-judge rounds, each re-deriving the oracle independently. The engine was judged behaviorally correct in every round; all three earlier failures were in my verification, and each was material. Round two found the whole suite bound one level below the contract's subject, asserting an in-memory array where every frozen Then is a claim about what the guard prints and what the run exits with; nine plausible wrong implementations shipped green through that gap. Round three found a plugin-root branch that survived the entire suite while misreporting a correctly-shipped component in this very repo. The final round ran twenty-six fresh mutants and found no live defect, verifying each of its five survivors dormant against the real tree rather than assuming. Across four independent sweeps roughly sixty distinct wrong implementations were run and every one that could misbehave on a real repository is caught. Two disagreements were resolved by reproduction rather than deference, one in each direction: the judge withdrew its allowlist correction, and it upheld my reading that the spec's Key terms outrank an implementation constant.

title: The manifest guard reports a clean run when its root is unusable
why: The node argues it exposes no report-only mode precisely because a chain that reports green over a defect is treated as clearance to commit. A root that names no directory, names a file, or is empty collapses into the same output as a genuinely clean tree — clean report, exit zero — because the directory read swallows every error. That is the same green-over-a-defect the node rules out, so it contradicts a completion claim this mission made. It cannot fire in this repository, whose chain passes a fixed root, but the guard ships to consumers that will not. Closing it is one check that the root resolves to a readable directory, and the frozen suite specifies nothing here, so it needs a scenario first.

title: The manifest guard's suite names no pointer inside an array
why: Twelve of this repository's live pointers sit in an array under one key, and array traversal is implemented and unit-bound but reaches no frozen scenario. Deleting the traversal left every per-scenario check green while silently dropping all twelve. The engine is correct; the contract is thinner than the implementation, so a later refactor could remove the behavior without the suite objecting. An additive scenario self-clears and needs no re-open.

title: Two documented fail-open behaviors in the manifest guard have no binding
why: Both under-report when broken and both are stated in the node's own key terms: the walk up to the nearest package manifest above a plugin root, and the skip of dependency and version-control directories during discovery. Neither can fire in this repository — every plugin root carries its own package manifest and no dependency directory holds a manifest — so both are dormant regression risk rather than present defects. Two cheap fixtures bind them.

title: The shipped SDD judge agents are pinned to a model smaller than their own mandated load
why: Both judge agents pin a model whose context is smaller than the governance floor their own definitions require them to load, which runs to roughly a thousand lines before either opens a spec file. Two of six dispatches in this mission died outright, one mid-run and one at launch, and the single round that returned consumed more than that model holds and survived only by compacting. Every round that produced a verdict here needed a model override. This will recur for anyone running the loop against a corpus this size.

title: The plugin capability node predates the four required spec sections
why: The parent node is behavioral and carries only its use cases, missing the overview, control flow and scenario map the spec format requires. Pre-existing and out of scope for a guard change — widening a fix into a parent backfill is the scope creep the kill-or-ship lens exists to catch — but two judges flagged it independently, so it wants its own backfill.

title: One plugin duplicates its generated codex manifest where the others symlink it
why: Two plugins symlink that manifest to their canonical source, so it cannot drift; the third keeps a real copy that can. Checked at the time of writing and the copies agree on every component pointer, differing only in a vendor schema url, so this is drift risk rather than present drift. Making the third a symlink like its siblings removes the class.
